incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: P1 - High tail latency for tenant 'corp-acme' (dedicated-pool-7). Symptoms: request queueing, 95p latency > 1.2s, some timeouts. Pager triggered at 2025-11-06T09:00:00Z (ts=1749301200)

Alice (oncall): I'm on it. Noted tenant is on a dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-7) and it's the only noisy tenant right now. Any recent deploys?

Mike (SE): No deploys in the last 6h for that tenant. CSM (Sarah) reports customer reports saw errors starting ~09:00 UTC.

Sarah (CSM): Confirmed — customer says high latency on embeddings/streaming generate paths, especially for long prompts. They started a campaign at 08:58 that likely explains spike.

Tara (platform): Looking at pool metrics: worker busy fraction spiked to 98%, queue length jumped to ~320 requests. Batching latency increased; backlog of KV-cache warmups.

Javier (infra): Logs show large batch assembly attempts with max_batch_tokens set to 2048 for this tenant. We're seeing few huge batches that block smaller low-latency requests. Sample log: ```
[09:01:12] pool=dedicated-pool-7 tenant=corp-acme assemble_batch id=0 size=14 total_tokens=18240 max_batch_tokens=2048 wait_ms=250
[09:01:12] pool=dedicated-pool-7 dispatch delay=230ms
[09:01:13] pool=dedicated-pool-7 queue_length=312```

Alice (oncall): That explains it. Large token caps are causing big starts-before-send behavior. We need a targeted mitigation for corp-acme only — can't throttle whole pool. What knobs can we flip live?

Tara (platform): We can adjust per-tenant scheduler knobs via the control plane: `max_batch_tokens`, `max_batch_size`, and `batch_wait_ms`. Also we can enable per-tenant queue_priority or set a per-tenant max_inflight_requests to bound occupancy.

Mike (SE): Proposed quick mitigation (goal: reduce tail latency without dropping throughput too much):
1) Reduce max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 512 for corp-acme.
2) Lower max_batch_size from 16 -> 8.
3) Reduce batch_wait_ms from 250 -> 50 to flush smaller batches earlier.
4) Enable per-tenant backpressure: set max_inflight_requests=60.

Alice (oncall): Sounds good. Is this safe to apply live? Any risk of increased token cost or regressions?

Mike (SE): It will likely increase per-token overhead slightly (less batch efficiency) but will significantly reduce head/tail latency for small/medium requests. For corp-acme's campaign, latency is the priority. We'll roll back after peak.

Javier (infra): I'll apply the control change to the tenant via the admin API now. Command I'm going to run:```
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood.local/admin/tenants/corp-acme/tuning" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '
{
  "max_batch_tokens": 512,
  "max_batch_size": 8,
  "batch_wait_ms": 50,
  "max_inflight_requests": 60
}
'```
I'll push and confirm config diff.

ops-bot: config-change: tenant=corp-acme user=javier@redwood.example action=update_tuning started at 2025-11-06T09:02:18Z

Javier (infra): Pushed. Control plane returned 200 and diff shows old->new. Applying to pool routing; streaming workers will pick up config on next reconcile (within ~5s).

Tara (platform): Workers acknowledged new config: `reconcile tenant=corp-acme new.max_batch_tokens=512 new.max_batch_size=8 new.batch_wait_ms=50`

Alice (oncall): Monitoring metrics now.

(30s later)

Tara (platform): Immediate effect: queue length down to 80, busy fraction ~72%, 95p latency dropped from 1.2s -> 340ms. No increase in 5xx.

Sarah (CSM): Customer confirms improved response times in their UX. They saw errors stop and streaming latency improved. :thumbsup:

Mike (SE): To be safe, let's also add a short-lived rule to deprioritize very large-batch jobs from this tenant while campaign runs. We can set `max_batch_tokens_strict=true` for 30m so scheduler refuses assembling batches >512 tokens.

Javier (infra): Applying `max_batch_tokens_strict` flag now.```
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood.local/admin/tenants/corp-acme/tuning/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"max_batch_tokens_strict": true, "expires_in": 1800}'```
ops-bot: flag-change: tenant=corp-acme user=javier@redwood.example flag=max_batch_tokens_strict=true expires=1800s

Alice (oncall): Good. Next steps: 1) Keep config for 1 hour while campaign finishes, 2) follow up with capacity/SE to recommend long-term tuning or a dedicated queue for heavy runs, 3) create runbook note. Who owns follow-ups?

Mike (SE): I'll draft a recommendation for corp-acme: either schedule large offline batch jobs into a separate pool or use smaller chunking on client side. I'll send recommended tuning and cost tradeoffs.

Sarah (CSM): I'll coordinate with the customer about scheduling future campaigns and offer guidance on chunking and cadence.

Tara (platform): I'll create an automatic detection rule to alert if per-tenant max_batch_tokens saturates repeatedly (>= 10 times in 1h). We should auto-suggest lowering tokens or creating a separate queue.

Alice (oncall): Great. Marking incident as mitigated. I'll close the pager but keep ticket open for postmortem and runbook updates.

incident-bot: Pager P1 (1749301200) status: mitigated -> monitoring. Closed by Alice (oncall) at 2025-11-06T09:06:05Z (ts=1749301565)

Alice (oncall): Postmortem action items: 
- [Mike] Draft tenant tuning recommendation for corp-acme (due EOD).
- [Tara] Add auto-detect rule for max_batch_tokens saturation (due +3d).
- [Javier] Add one-click control to enforce `max_batch_tokens_strict` in console (due +5d).
- [Sarah] Customer follow-up around campaign scheduling (due +1d).

Mike (SE): A note for the runbook: example rapid mitigation snippet to reduce latency:
```
# quick mitigation (admin API)
PATCH /admin/tenants/{tenant}/tuning
{
  "max_batch_tokens": 512,
  "max_batch_size": 8,
  "batch_wait_ms": 50,
  "max_inflight_requests": 60
}
# optional strict enforcement
POST /admin/tenants/{tenant}/tuning/flags
{
  "max_batch_tokens_strict": true,
  "expires_in": 1800
}
```

Alice (oncall): Thanks team. Closing thread after follow-ups created in PagerDuty/Ticketing.
